text:
Nashville has won four straight, and the Predators did it this time the way they did it for most of the last decade: Roman Josi running the game from the back end and Juuse Saros refusing to blink. Josi played 25:36, had two assists, and was on the ice for 2.02 expected goals for and 0.66 against. Saros made 25 saves and stopped 1.3 more goals than his shots deserved, the most wins added by anyone in the building.

St. Louis started well enough. Jimmy Snuggerud scored on the power play at 13:07 of the first, set up by Philip Broberg and Robert Thomas. Three minutes later Steven Stamkos answered on Nashville's power play, two nights after his overtime winner in Colorado, with Mavrik Bourque and Josi on the play. The goal that swung it came from the bottom of the lineup: Ross Colton, in 11:24 of ice time, snapped one in at 9:02 of the second off Jack Drury, moving Nashville from 52% to 72% in our win model. Nick Perbix closed it with 1:29 left on a 5% shot.

This wasn't a robbery. Nashville had the better chances, 2.95 expected goals to 2.28, and deserved the win 60% of the time. Joel Hofer did his part for the Blues, 26 saves and a stop on Filip Forsberg in the second that was the biggest save of the day, but St. Louis managed 0.56 expected goals in the third while chasing.

The streak lines up with a roster that has been shaken: Matthew Wood went to Seattle for Shane Wright on November 1, Ryan O'Reilly's name keeps coming up in trade talk, and the wins keep coming anyway. Nashville is now 2-0 against St. Louis this season after a 5-2 win in October. The Blues, coming off a comeback from 4-1 down in New Jersey that still ended in a loss, got the effort back and none of the goals.
headline: Josi and Saros, still the Predators' engine
